findings.obligation: Architectural test T1 / law L8 as recorded: 'The check governs the whole set of pre-paint scripts, so it must still refuse a third one added later', and the layer's own doc comment claims 'a third pre-paint script added later is governed the moment the head references it' (nw-type-level-design: claim only the strength the checker gives; name each bypass the change leaves open).
findings.observation: Set membership is decided by three narrow source substrings: the asset must contain 'localStorage.getItem' or 'sessionStorage.getItem' AND one of 'documentElement.setAttribute', 'documentElement.removeAttribute', 'documentElement.dataset'. A third pre-paint asset that reads the stored choice by bracket access (window.localStorage['foundry.x']), through a local alias (var store = window.localStorage; store.getItem(...)), or that stamps through an element reference (var root = document.documentElement; root.setAttribute(...)) reads stored state and stamps the document element, yet does NOT qualify, so defer/async/type=module on its tag is accepted silently. The layer's fail-closed arm cannot catch that case either: it fires only when the qualifying set is EMPTY, and the two shipped assets keep the count at 2 forever. Checked against the shipped assets: theme.js and nav-collapse.js both match, so the law governs today's set and the gate is green (my run 1), but the 'third one added later' half of T1 holds only for an asset written in the same idioms.
findings.remediation: Widen the membership test to the idiom-independent pair -- the asset's comment-stripped source contains 'localStorage' or 'sessionStorage' at all AND contains 'documentElement' at all -- which still excludes every shipped deferred neighbour (none of them names localStorage), or, if a narrower test is wanted, state the idiom limit in the layer's doc comment instead of claiming that a later script is governed the moment the head references it.

Implementation correctness, read line by line against the design's laws and claims. crates/foundry-app/static/js/nav-collapse.js: interpret(value) is 'value === COLLAPSED', total over every string and over null, so L5 holds by construction and no stored value can be refused or throw; remember() writes the single sentinel or removeItem, never a word for expanded (C2); applyMarker sets the attribute to the EMPTY string or removes it, never a value (C1), and every consuming selector in foundry.4c73f62c.css (lines 1020, 1025, 1030-1032, 1035, 1041, and the phone arms at 1362, 1366, 1371) matches on [data-nav-collapsed] presence with no value anywhere -- the crafter-declared review obligation C1 is satisfied; stored() and remember() each wrap the localStorage touch in try/catch and return/ignore (B1, B2, Y1); applyMarker runs at head-parse time, before buildToggle, which is why the marker is on the document before paint; buildToggle returns early when .sidebar__brand is absent (B4, Y3) and is the ONLY place the button exists, so no server-side path can render a dead control (C3) -- templates/partials/sidebar.html adds exactly one id attribute and no element, so the crafter-declared obligation C3 is satisfied; paint() re-derives aria-expanded, aria-label and title from the boolean on every press, so the name can never describe the previous state; a document load never calls remember(), so L3's 'a load never rewrites the key' holds; no storage event listener exists, so L1's two-tab divergence is the admitted state the oracle asserts. The asset is a straight-line guarded IIFE in the same procedural shape as the frozen theme.js port, which is the paradigm of the surface it joins. No untrusted string reaches the DOM, no innerHTML, no secret, no path or command handling.

Design quality, procedural paradigm (the bound paradigm; the universal craftsmanship axes apply and no class catalogue does). Owners: the collapse state, the storage key, the sentinel and both effects have exactly one owner, static/js/nav-collapse.js; the marker is the one channel to the stylesheet; theme.js is untouched and stays a byte-identical port, so no second owner of a navigation state was created. Each unit does one thing (interpret, stored, remember, applyMarker, describe, buildToggle, paint). Boundaries: nothing in Rust reads or writes the choice, so no route, handler, migration, secret, URL, DNS name or FOUNDRY_ setting enters the feature and deployment independence holds by construction. The contract agreement moves in one diff: the renamed blob, base.html line 6, the three static_cache_policy_tests assertions and the VENDOR.md row and prose are all updated in this commit and the gate recomputes the digest from the committed bytes. Type-level: the carrier is a boolean and the marker is valueless, so a third rail geometry is unrepresentable by centralised construction rather than by a runtime check -- the honest strength for JavaScript with no static checker, which the ADR states as such, and the bypass (a later edit rewriting a selector to match a VALUE) is named and left as a standing review obligation rather than claimed as proved. The new xtask layer is a free function beside the other check_arch layers with its two fixtures in the file's existing style, and LAYER_1_RULE_MARKERS grew to 16 with 'pre-paint-script:' added, so the shipped silent-disarm guard covers it. ACCEPTED, with five non-blocking findings routed to their owners. No blocker and no critical finding.

WHAT I JUDGED, INDEPENDENTLY. The whole-candidate diff 49701b8..e4220d6 against the immutable oracle crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/nav-collapse-toggle.feature, the consumed design (architecture.md, ADR-NAV-COLLAPSE-001, the eight laws and three construction claims), the acceptance brief's rows and the original Request. I formed my own questions and read every changed byte of production, oracle, support, gate and document; I consumed no producer or embedded review record.

IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTNESS. The mechanism is correct at the level the design claims. interpret() is one equality over a single key, total over every string and over the absence of the key, so an outside writer's value can never be refused and can never throw. remember() writes the single sentinel or removes the key, so expanded has exactly one stored form, the absence that the no-JavaScript promise rests on. applyMarker() writes the attribute with an EMPTY value or removes it, and every one of the nine consuming selectors in foundry.4c73f62c.css matches on [data-nav-collapsed] PRESENCE, so the third rail geometry is unrepresentable by centralised construction -- the crafter-declared obligation C1 is satisfied. The control exists only in script and templates/partials/sidebar.html adds exactly one inert id attribute and no element, so there is no server-side path to a dead control -- the crafter-declared obligation C3 is satisfied. Both storage touches are guarded, buildToggle returns early on an absent mount point, a document load never writes the key, no storage event listener exists, and the accessible name and aria-expanded are re-derived from the boolean on every press. The asset keeps the straight-line guarded-IIFE shape of the surface it joins, which is the bound procedural paradigm, and theme.js stays byte-identical.
